findings.assertion: The December 1928 law did more than eliminate elected councils: according to the 2009 constitutional analysis, its first twenty articles specified the Department Central and thirteen delegations through streets, railways, bridges, hills and canals. The 1928 demarcation therefore requires historical cartography, not a projection of current alcaldía boundaries.
findings.source_locator: Hurtado and Arellano 2009 p.217, numbered points 2-4; Carmona HTML paragraph on 1928 Ley Orgánica
findings.limitations: The original Dec 31 1928 DOF articles 1-20 and signed maps not examined; retrospective may compress legal sequence

findings.assertion: The 31 December 1941 law replaced the earlier Department Central division with a City of Mexico and twelve political delegations, maintaining federal legislative control; this intermediate 1941 period must not disappear between accounts of 1928 and 1970.
findings.source_locator: Hurtado and Arellano 2009 pp.217-218 section 2.5; Pavón González thesis printed p.28
findings.limitations: Original 1941 DOF law and boundary plan not inspected; no current-site physical attribution

findings.assertion: The 31 December 1970 legal reorganization expanded the Federal District from twelve to sixteen delegations, adding central jurisdictions Cuauhtémoc, Miguel Hidalgo, Benito Juárez and Venustiano Carranza; the published 2009 study ties the new borders to Article 11 of that law.
findings.source_locator: Hurtado and Arellano 2009 pp.218-219 section 2.6; Pavón González thesis printed p.28
findings.limitations: Law issued 31 Dec 1970 versus 1971 administrative implementation needs original decrees; no mapping from 1970 to present borders verified

findings.assertion: The constitutional analysis identifies a 31 December 1972 organic-law revision that modified boundaries of the sixteen delegations created under the 1970 arrangement. A walk or map keyed only to the 1970 version would conflate two distinct legal geographies.
findings.limitations: Original 1972 law and historical boundary map not checked; geographic impact not quantified

findings.assertion: The 10 August 1987 reform established an elected Federal District Assembly with 40 majority-seat and 26 proportional-representation members, but Congress retained general legislative authority for the District; an elected assembly did not yet amount to a locally elected head of government.
findings.source_locator: Hurtado and Arellano 2009 p.219 section 2.8, 40+26 seats and restricted powers
findings.limitations: Original 1987 decree and inaugural legislative debates not checked; assembly site at time not verified

findings.assertion: A 1987 UNAM architectural thesis reporting on DDF planning calculations lists approximately 123,000 square metres of central-administration space, 10,900 office workers, and an estimated 36,300-square-metre deficit. These are contemporary planning estimates, not verified measurements for 2026.
findings.source_locator: Pavón González 1987 thesis printed pp.10-11, central office dimensioning and 1973 study attribution
findings.limitations: Underlying 1973 DDF equipment survey not examined; estimates may reflect different dates and typologies; cannot infer actual building footprint

findings.assertion: The same architectural thesis records 48,250 square metres of decentralized delegación office floor space, 4,700 employees and a projected 14,200-square-metre deficit for 1978, illustrating that the 1970 governance reform created a second, physically distributed demand for offices.
findings.source_locator: Pavón González thesis printed p.11, decentralized office statistics
findings.limitations: Historical estimates as presented by thesis; no original official space register; proposed architecture not proof of eventual construction

findings.assertion: The 1987 thesis judged some delegación offices poorly placed relative to population and transport, naming Coyoacán, Miguel Hidalgo and Álvaro Obregón among examples; it also says other delegations could not simply widen roads or relocate offices without damage to historic-character neighborhoods.
findings.source_locator: Pavón González thesis printed p.11, subsections Ubicación and Calidad de la edificación
findings.limitations: Author's planning judgment not proof that any specific historic building survived; underlying 1973 DDF survey and photographs missing

findings.assertion: The thesis distinguishes ordinary delegación technical offices from Civil Registry and neighborhood-board functions that needed ceremonial and representative space; it also describes semiurban Álvaro Obregón subdelegations as social-assistance and agricultural-information points. Administrative geography was reflected in the type of rooms residents encountered.
findings.source_locator: Pavón González thesis original scanned printed p.13, items 2 and 3; screenshot reviewed
findings.limitations: Author's design diagnosis, not a verified visitor route or surviving room inventory; no 1980s municipal budget or registry floor plans checked

findings.assertion: In Matos Moctezuma's published first-person retrospective, the initial 1978 Coyolxauhqui rescue included five offerings near the disk, and Raúl Arana and Rafael Domínguez inspected the discovery for Salvamento Arqueológico. Barrera Rodríguez's later overview instead names Ángel García Cook and Raúl Arana as responders; these may refer to different steps and must not be silently harmonized.
findings.source_locator: Matos article indexed paragraph on first five offerings and named field visitors; Barrera article indexed paragraph on initial responders
findings.limitations: Neither the original 1978 field log nor full text of both later accounts inspected; the personnel discrepancy requires chronology before definitive attribution

findings.assertion: Barrera Rodríguez dates the beginning of the Proyecto Templo Mayor excavation campaign to 20 March 1978 and describes six of seven construction stages observable from the archaeological visitor entrance at the time of his publication. The statement describes the older visitor route, not a verified 2026 itinerary.
findings.source_locator: Barrera Rodríguez, Arqueología Mexicana especial 79 pp.32-35, indexed opening two paragraphs; Matos indexed history of excavation
findings.limitations: Full article page images and original site phase drawings not inspected; route and number of visible stages require 2026 physical checks
